item.title: Contributor: woodpeck Discussion Comment No.: 15 Comment: As a general remark: The fact that a Wikidata entry links to an OSM object is NEVER a reason not to delete or renumber the OSM object. OSM mappers are not responsible for updating Wikidata; linking to hard-coded OSM IDs is not recommended for precisely this reason. Date: 2026-03-20T21:21:51+01:00

Contributor: leveskockaa Discussion Comment No.: 1 Comment: Hello! Next time you map a new business opening in place of an old one, please reuse the node of the old business (in this case, https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/6447258236) so that the history (https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/6447258236/history) is visible and provides other mappers with the extra information needed to decide if it's an error, or their information is outdated. https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/1758991234/history is a good example of the node history being accessible and providing more information. Date: 2026-03-20T07:33:58+01:00

Contributor: Anas masuris Discussion Comment No.: 19 Comment: So, there exists no rule, that says that "the track having entry signals must be tagged with usage=*" and yet you say that it is a must based on exemplary graphic... Mhm. Sorry, but this is not a rule which has been agreed on, but only your interpretation. The only things stated on this page are: * The key usage=* is used to identify the primary usage of a railway track * Inside a railway station area, use usage=main or usage=branch only for the main tracks (not for siding, yard tracks etc.) It may be true for German railways (Still there are non-compliant examples in DE as well, but hush hush), but it doesn't imply automatically that in other countries it is 1:1, given how different regulations and classification is. So the only thing I have to say is to follow the other countries tagging schemes, not reflecting the German one Date: 2026-03-15T19:55:10+01:00
